brief.scope: Author independent startup tests for conduct and prepare_conductor using conductor-start-plan.md, permission-surface.md, harness-capabilities.md and the supplied approved interfaces. Own only ops/conductor/tests/test_conduct_start.py, test_conduct_enforcement.py and conduct_test_support.py. Cover CLI forms, configurable harness/model/role/profile, exact admitted tokens and fixed refusals, full descriptor validation, untrusted matching digests, actual-client MCP versus separate server checks, partial valid onboarding without path hints, canonical delegation, forbidden handwork and launch/resume binding before effects. Use verified synthetic counterparties and faulty controls; no real harness, credentials or live admission. Do not read/write implementation or invent missing protocols. Collect assertion reds against absent source and report any genuinely undeclared boundary. Record hashes/commands/coverage. Grok-only trailers; inline envelope note at most 1000 words.

findings.claim: prepare_conductor takes trusted_context as a direct in-process argument or inherited read-only descriptor, never a caller path, environment variable, model tool argument or MCP parameter, but the CLI inheritance channel for that descriptor is unnamed. Tests therefore prove composition in-process and only use subprocess CLI for argv grammar and pre-effect refusals.

prepare_conductor returns the descriptor and the adapter's compiled launch, but the packaging (2-tuple versus a closed mapping and the compiled-launch key name) is unnamed. Tests accept a 2-tuple or a mapping with keys descriptor and compiled_launch, recorded as PIN_PREPARE_RETURN.

normalize_tool consumes a native_request whose closed schema is not declared; only surfaces (edit/apply_patch, Git, shell, vendor, in-session agent) are named. Tests use PIN_NATIVE_REQUEST {surface,argv,cwd,environment,executable}.

conduct-config is named for malformed or untrusted descriptor transport with secret-free fixed reasons and a doctor remedy, but unlike conduct-argv and conduct-mcp it has no exact expected/found/needed template. Tests assert the wire, class token and doctor in needed.

Startup must verify initialize, tools/list and tools/call lane_start from the actual client after child creation; a separate CLI query is not proof. How those client bytes are observed (server-side log, intercepted stdio, or another handle) is unnamed. Tests attach a FakeMcpClient to the in-process context.

evaluate_tool's bound_role is a verified handle to the descriptor, policy binding and admitted tool declarations, and delegate/read arguments are the target owner's validated structured request, without closed JSON shapes here. Tests pin a mapping with descriptor_sha256, binding and tools, and delegate arguments {job:author-tests}.
